notes: Everything below was declared BEFORE any XYLD bar was captured. The adverse threshold of -1.5% rather than SPY's -2% reflects an equity beta recalled at 0.6 to 0.8, so a day that is a stress day for the S&P 500 moves this fund less; it was chosen on that reasoning and not from any XYLD return.

cost.source: commission-free US ETF; half spread and slippage DECLARED, wider than SPY's because a covered-call fund's book is thinner, and not measured

monitor.variable: VIX minus the 21-day realised volatility of the S&P 500
monitor.source: CBOE publishes VIX daily and FRED distributes it; realised volatility is computed from sealed S&P 500 prices

survival.counterparty: buyers of S&P 500 call options, who pay for upside exposure that the fund sells them inside the wrapper
survival.why_they_accept_losing: they want convex upside at limited cost, and structured product issuers hedge by buying calls, so demand for upside is not sensitive to price; the premium is what the sellers earn for taking the other side of that demand and for bearing the crash risk it implies
survival.what_would_end_it: realised volatility persistently exceeding implied, so that selling upside stops being paid, or enough capital selling calls to compress implied volatility below what is realised -- which is what the declared monitor watches for
